name: Gautama Buddha
dates_notes: The chronology of the historical Buddha remains disputed. This broad fifth-century BCE placement follows the range commonly used in modern scholarship and is not a claim for any single traditional dating.
evidence_basis: Teachings transmitted in the early Buddhist canons and parallel recensions; no autograph text survives.
own_corpus_survival: No autograph corpus; early teachings survive in transmitted Pāli, Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan canons and parallels.
core_thesis: The Buddha is the canonical teacher around whom the early Buddhist traditions preserve a path organized by the diagnosis and cessation of suffering. The early transmitted discourses present dependent arising, impermanence, and the analysis of persons and experience without a permanent self as mutually connected tools for loosening craving and ignorance. Because the materials are recensional and the historical teacher left no autograph treatise, this entry represents a canonical teaching corpus rather than a recoverable authorial system in the later scholastic sense.
